name: status
title: Connection status
description: Lists the Figma files whose Pixelwright plugin is connected (name, current page, editor, whether Allow edits is on) and marks the active one: the file whose plugin window was in front last, which every tool uses when no file is named. Call it first, and whenever a tool says no file is connected: hint says what to do. While a plugin waits to be paired, pairing holds the code: tell the user to type it into the Pixelwright window, and never type or send it yourself. probe: true also pings the active file's plugin.

probe.description: Also ping the active file's plugin and report the round trip.

name: selection_get
title: Read the selection
description: Lists the layers the user selected in Figma (id, name, type, box in page coordinates). Call it when the user says "this", "the selected one" or "what I picked", then read those ids with design_read or outline.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: node_show
title: Show layers
description: Brings layers into view in Figma (switching to their page when needed) and selects them, so the user sees what you mean: one layer, or several on one page, fitted in view or at a zoom (1 is 100%) centred on them; select: false only moves the view. Changes only the view and the selection, never the file.

node.description: The layer's id, e.g. 54:243. Give node or nodes.

nodes.description: Several layers on one page, fitted in view together.

select.description: Select them too (default), or only bring them into view.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: selection_wait
title: Wait for a selection
description: Waits until the user selects something in Figma, then answers with the selection, as selection_get does (changed: false when the time ran out first). Tell the user what to select before calling it: "select the card you mean in Figma".

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the user to select something: 60 by default, 300 at most.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

changed.description: Whether the user selected something else before the time ran out.

name: changes_since
title: What changed
description: What changed in the file since the plugin started watching (its window opened) or since an earlier answer's cursor: each layer created, deleted or changed (with the properties), by the user, a collaborator or Pixelwright itself, on the page the user was on. Ask with no cursor once to start, then with the cursor it gives, to read again only what the designer changed. Only pages the user had open while the plugin ran are watched; an edit made while one of Pixelwright's writes runs (or within a second after) counts as Pixelwright's, and changes from code execute left running count as the user's. What changed while the plugin was closed, and token values, baseline_diff tells against a saved baseline.

cursor.description: The cursor an earlier answer gave: only what changed after it. Default: all the plugin has seen.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: file_map
title: Map the file
description: Every page of the file with its top layers (frames, sections, components) and, inside each section, its own, with their types and sizes, in one call: where to start in a big file. Pages load one at a time; past the time a call has, more: true and the rest are left out (outline them one by one).

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: viewport_get
title: What the user sees
description: What the user is looking at in Figma now: the page, the zoom, the part of the page in view (page px), and the page's layers and their children that meet it, outermost first. Use it when the user says "this" or "here" without selecting anything; selection_get gives what is selected.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: nodes_find
title: Find layers
description: Finds layers on the current page, or inside `within`, by name (substring), type (FRAME, TEXT, INSTANCE…), text content (substring) or component (an instance's component or component set name). Returns ids, names, types, boxes and the names of their ancestors, at most `limit` (more: true when there were more). Combine criteria to narrow down.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: outline
title: Outline a frame
description: The layer tree of a frame, a page or the current page, as light XML: tag (the Figma type), id, name and box (x and y relative to the outlined node) per layer, to `depth` levels; an instance also names its component and variant, so repeated components show. Use it to find the sections of a big frame before reading one with design_read. A layer with `$children="N"` has N children not listed here: outline it on its own.

node.description: The layer or page id, or 0:0 for the list of pages. Default: the current page.

depth.description: How many levels below the node to list (1 to 10).

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

nodes.description: How many layers the XML lists.

name: nodes_delete
title: Delete layers
description: Deletes layers by id, each on its own: one Figma will not delete (a layer inside an instance, which comes from its component: hide it with display="none" in design_apply instead) stays, with why. One call is one undo step in Figma. Refused while the plugin's Allow edits switch is off.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: screenshot
title: Screenshot a layer
description: Renders a layer to PNG so you can see it: a section to build, or your result to check. Returned inline at most 2000 px on a side: a larger layer comes scaled down to fit, and the text says its full size. For details of a tall layer screenshot one section of it (outline lists them), or pass clip for a region of it; pass save to write the PNG full size to a file instead.

scale.description: Pixels per Figma pixel: 2 for a sharp look, below 1 to fit.

effects.description: Include shadows and outside strokes around the layer; false renders only its own box.

save.description: Write the PNG to this file (any size) instead of returning it; a relative path is from the server's folder.

clip.description: Only this region of the layer, in Figma px from its box's top left (before scale); with effects on it may reach into what paints around the box.

modes.description: Render in these variable modes, by collection and mode name, e.g. {"Theme": "Dark"}: set on the layer for the render, then set back (needs Allow edits; the file is left as it was).

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: design_read
title: Read a design
description: Reads a layer (a section, a card, a screen) as Pixelwright's XML: Figma's layer types as tags, Image and Icon for true assets, CSS properties as attributes (var(--Name) where Figma binds a style or variable), ids to read or change a layer later. The first text block is the XML; the second is JSON with tokens (their values), textStyles, fonts, assets (written to assetsDir when given), hints on what the code should bind, truncated (ids of branches left empty to fit maxChars: read each on its own), measurements (the designer's Dev Mode measurements in px) and motion (Figma Motion as CSS @keyframes, a layer's summary being $motion in the XML) when there are any, and, where the project has Figma Code Connect templates (*.figma.ts), codeComponents: the code connected instances render to ({ids, component, template, snippet, imports}, the same code once), with imports and codeErrors; such an instance is $code in the XML, without its children: use its code as it is (code: false reads it as layers). A layer with position absolute is placed against its parent element: give that parent position: relative. For a big frame, find its sections with outline first. Rebuild the result with the project's own components and tokens.

node.description: The layer's id, e.g. 54:243. Default: the one layer selected in Figma.

depth.description: Levels below the layer to read. Default: all.

assetsDir.description: Folder to write the icons (SVG) and images (PNG at 2x, originals for backgrounds) into, e.g. src/assets; the XML's src paths start with it. Without it the assets are only planned.

screenshot.description: Also return the layer's image, to compare your build with.

maxChars.description: Longest XML to return; deeper branches past it come back empty with $truncated, to read on their own.

code.description: Run the project's Code Connect templates, giving connected instances as $code with their code (default); false reads them as layers.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: inspect
title: Inspect layers
description: Reads layers as Figma has them, for what design_read's CSS cannot say, without running code (works while Allow edits is off): the layout box and the painted box (centred or outside strokes, shadows and blur reach past it), the fill as a CSS value with the paint style or variables behind it (what a var() in design_read resolves to), how strokes paint (align, per-side weights, dashes, whether auto layout counts them), every effect with Figma's own parameters (a progressive blur's start and end, noise, texture), a text's lines with what ended each (Enter or Shift+Enter) and its line heights (px, auto, percent), how far a layer overflows its parent, its prototype interactions (trigger, destination, transition, duration, easing) and its component's variant. Boxes are measured from relativeTo's top left, so it also measures: give a list of layers and their section.

nodes.description: The layers' ids, e.g. ["54:243"]. Default: the layers selected in Figma.

relativeTo.description: A layer (a section, a frame) whose top left the boxes are measured from. Default: the page's.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

relativeTo.description: What the boxes are measured from: a layer as `id "name"`, or the page.

paintedBox.description: What is painted, when it differs from the box: centred or outside strokes, shadows, blur.

overflow.description: How far the layer reaches past the room its parent gives it, in px.

effects.description: Every effect with Figma's own parameters.

css.description: The fill as a CSS value, top paint first: a colour, a gradient as Figma writes it.

style.description: The paint style it comes from, and the token design_read names it by.

tokens.description: The variables the paints are bound to, by token, with their values.

missing.description: Ids that are not layers of this file.

left.description: Layers asked for past the first 100, not read: inspect them next.

name: nodes_diff
title: Compare two layers
description: Compares two layers (A/B variants of a screen, a card and its copy) as design_read reads them: layers are matched by their path of names below each root (same-named siblings in order), and the answer lists the layers only A or only B has, and for each layer both have, the attributes that differ as [A's, B's] (text as $text, an instance's variant and props too) and whether an icon's or image's own drawing differs (paths, colours, inner layers). Ids and the two roots' own names and places are left out. Works while Allow edits is off. To compare a layer with how it was when you built it, use baseline_diff.

a.description: The first layer's id (variant A), e.g. 54:243.

depth.description: Levels below each layer to compare. Default: all.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

drawing.description: An icon's or image's own drawing differs: paths, colours, inner layers.

more.description: Differences past the ones listed: compare smaller parts of the two layers.

name: baseline_save
title: Keep a baseline
description: Keeps a layer as you build code from it, so baseline_diff can tell later what the designer changed: its read and the values of the tokens it uses, in every mode, go into .pixelwright/baselines/<name>.json in the project (it holds the design's texts: commit the folder to share it, or leave it out of git). Save right after the design_read you build a screen or section from; name it after your code (pricing, plan-card) and list in code the files you build from it. Once your code has the changes a baseline_diff listed, pass the accept it gave: exactly the design it compared is kept, so what the designer changed after it still shows next time. An existing name is replaced only with accept or replace: true; code alone changes its file list. Writes nothing to Figma, so it works while Allow edits is off.

node.description: The layer the code is built from: a frame, section, component or instance. Default: the one selected layer. Not with accept.

name.description: Named after the code: pricing, plan-card. Default: the layer's name as a slug. Required with accept.

code.description: The project's files built from the layer, relative to the project. Default: the list the baseline already has.

accept.description: The accept a baseline_diff answer gave: keeps exactly the design that diff compared.

replace.description: Start the named baseline over from the layer as it is now. Not with accept.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

page.description: Null from a plugin older than this server.

capturedAt.description: When the design it keeps was read (the diff's read, with accept).

tokens.description: Variables and styles kept with their values in every mode.

cut.description: Branches the read did not hold whole: baseline_diff does not compare inside them.

replaced.description: With replace: what the baseline it replaced kept, and how much the new read took in.

name: baseline_diff
title: What changed since a baseline
description: What the designer changed since baseline_save, in design_read's terms: each layer changed (its attributes as [before, after], a text's content as XML), added (with its XML when short), removed or hidden, moved to another parent or reordered; a change made in a component once, with the instances it reached and how many were compared (of); tokens whose value changed in any mode, renamed, newly used or no longer used; icons and images drawn anew (drawing: export them again). Layers are followed by id, a replaced one by its name. It sees what changes_since and Figma's own Changed mark miss: edits made while the plugin was closed, accepted library updates, variable and style values. Without name: every baseline in the project with how much changed; call it when a session starts or the user says the design changed. It reads the file the baseline came from and works while Allow edits is off. Change only the code it names (code lists the files), then call baseline_save with the accept it gives.

name.description: One baseline in detail. Without it: every baseline in the project, with how much changed.

node.description: Compare with this layer instead of the baseline's own, e.g. a v2 the designer made beside it. Needs name.

file.description: With name: compare in this file (a session from status, or a file name). Without name: only this file's baselines. Default: the file each baseline came from.

now.description: Compared with another layer: node, or the root found again by name.

reason.description: Missing, hidden, unavailable: what happened, and what to do.

accept.description: Pass it to baseline_save once your code has these changes.

more.description: Baselines past 50, or entries past 200 in one list.

name: breakpoints_find
title: Find a screen's other widths
description: Finds the screen a layer is on at the page's other widths (Desktop, Tablet, Mobile): the page's frames, and those in its sections, whose names match once size words are left out (Desktop, Mobile, 1440, 375px) and whose children share names with it, narrowest first, each with a score. Compare them with nodes_diff to write the media queries.

node.description: A screen's id, or a layer's on it.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

score.description: How alike the two are, 0 to 1: names without size words, and shared children.

widths.description: The screen at each width, narrowest first.

name: image_compare
title: Compare a layer with an image
description: Renders a layer as screenshot does (scale, effects and clip alike) and compares it with a PNG on disk, typically a screenshot of your build at the same size: rmse (0 to 255) and the share of differing pixels over the part both cover, the box around the differences, and the edges: each horizontal (rows, by y) and vertical (columns, by x) edge of the reference matched, shifted by a few px (by: how far the render's is off), missing, or extra in the render. diff writes a PNG of the difference. Take the reference at the render's density (scale 2 for a 2x screenshot). Works while Allow edits is off.

reference.description: The PNG to compare with, e.g. a screenshot of your build at the same size: a path, relative to the server's folder or absolute.

scale.description: Pixels per Figma pixel of the render: the reference's density.

effects.description: Render shadows and outside strokes around the layer; false renders only its own box.

clip.description: Only this region of the layer, in Figma px from its box's top left (before scale); with effects on it may reach into what paints around the box.

modes.description: Render in these variable modes, by collection and mode name, e.g. {"Theme": "Dark"}: set on the layer for the render, then set back (needs Allow edits; the file is left as it was).

diff.description: A .png path to write the difference to: the render faded, every differing pixel red.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

rmse.description: Root mean square colour difference, 0 to 255, both images over white.

different.description: The share of pixels that differ by more than antialiasing does, 0 to 1.

box.description: The box around every differing pixel, in px of the render; null when none differs.

rows.description: Horizontal edges by y: matched, shifted (by: + is lower in the render), missing, extra.

columns.description: Vertical edges by x: matched, shifted (by: + is further right in the render).

name: measure
title: Measure between layers
description: Measures the distances between layers, each from the one before it in the list (a→b, b→c, so a row's rhythm shows): the gap between their boxes on each axis (negative where they overlap), how their edges and centres line up (B's minus A's: 0 is aligned), and, when one holds the other, how far it sits from each edge, as padding. Layout boxes by default; painted: true measures what is painted (strokes, shadows). A sentence per pair says it plainly. Works while Allow edits is off.

nodes.description: The layers' ids in the order to measure, each from the one before, e.g. ["54:244", "54:268"]. Default: the layers selected in Figma.

painted.description: Measure what is painted (centred or outside strokes, shadows, blur) instead of the layout boxes.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

measured.description: The layout boxes, or what is painted (strokes and shadows included).

gap.description: The space between the two boxes on each axis, in px; negative where they overlap on that axis.

edges.description: B's edge minus A's, in px: 0 is aligned, positive is further right or lower.

contains.description: Which of the two holds the other within its box.

inset.description: How far the inner box sits from each edge of the outer one.

missing.description: Ids that are not layers of this file.

name: flow_read
title: Map the prototype
description: A page's prototype as a map, for an app's routes: where its flows start, its screens (the page's frames, and those in its sections) with their sizes, and every interaction that leaves its layer: from which screen and layer, on what trigger, to which screen (or back, close, a URL), and how it moves ("navigate to Detail; smart animate 300ms ease-out"). A variant switch stays inside its component and is read by design_read as $on-*.

page.description: The page's id. Default: the current page.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: contrast_check
title: Check text contrast
description: Rates every visible text under a layer for WCAG contrast against what is behind it (the layers below it that cover it, then its parents' fills, see-through ones laid over what is below): the ratio, whether it is large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold), and whether it passes AA and AAA. A text over an image or a gradient is said, not guessed: check those in a screenshot. Works while Allow edits is off.

node.description: The layer whose texts to check (a section, a screen). Default: the one layer selected in Figma.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

backdrop.description: The colour behind the text, or what it is when CSS cannot say ("an image", "a gradient").

ratio.description: The WCAG contrast ratio, 1 to 21; null when the backdrop is not one colour.

large.description: Large text in WCAG terms: 24 px, or 18.66 px at weight 700 or more.

name: fonts_check
title: Check the fonts
description: The fonts a layer's texts use (the selected layer's by default), by family with the weights used, and where the build gets each: whether Google Fonts serves it, with a ready css2 link for those weights, and the weights it lacks; a family Google Fonts does not have needs its own files. Google Fonts' public catalogue is read once (no key); offline, the fonts are still listed.

node.description: The layer whose texts' fonts to check (a section, a screen). Default: the one layer selected in Figma.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

weights.description: The weights used, "400 italic" for an italic.

google.description: Whether Google Fonts serves the family; null when it could not be reached.

css.description: The Google Fonts css2 link for the weights used.

name: design_audit
title: Audit the design's scale
description: The scale a layer uses (the selected layer by default): spacing (gaps and paddings), radii, font sizes, line heights and colours, each with how often it is used and whether it is bound to a token; and what is off it: values off the 4 px grid, raw colours equal to or a hair from a token, sizes a pixel apart. Use it to define tokens when a file has none, or to see what the build should round.

node.description: The layer to audit (a screen, a section). Default: the one layer selected in Figma.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

token.description: The variable these uses are bound to.

spacing.description: Gaps and paddings in px, smallest first.

token.description: The variable these uses are bound to.
The variable these uses are bound to.
The style or variable these uses are bound to.

colors.description: Fills, strokes and text colours, most used first; bound uses apart from raw ones.

name: tokens_usage
title: Where a token is used
description: The layers on the current page (or inside within) that use a style or variable, named by its token as design_read and tokens_read write it (--White-2 is the second style named White, --h1-font a text style), with where each uses it (fill, stroke, effect, text, a text run, or a bound field). Use it to tell same-named styles apart or to see what a change to a token would touch.

token.description: A style's or variable's token as design_read or tokens_read writes it: --White-2, --h1-font, --color-bg.

within.description: The layer or page to look in. Default: the current page.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

property.description: Where the layer uses it: fill, stroke, effect, text, a text run, or a field.

name: design_apply
title: Write a design
description: Writes Pixelwright XML, the format design_read returns, into Figma. An element with id changes that layer: only the attributes it gives, the rest stays as it is (write background="none", width="auto" to hug, display="block" to drop auto layout); under another parent, with before/after or in another order it moves the layer. An element without id creates a layer: Frame, Section, Text, Rectangle, Ellipse, Line; an Instance by component="Name" variant="Prop=Value" props="Label=Text"; a Component (prop and visibleProp on its layers make its properties) or a ComponentSet of Component variants; an Image or Icon from a file (src); copyOf="id" copies a layer and writes the element onto the copy. var(--Name) binds the style or variable of that name; note writes Dev Mode notes; fonts are loaded for you. XML read with design_read and sent back unchanged changes nothing. Each element is written on its own: errors come back with their line and attribute while the rest goes in, and the whole call is one undo step in Figma. The plugin refuses writes while its Allow edits switch is off (dryRun checks without writing). See guide write.

xml.description: Pixelwright XML, as design_read writes it: an element with id changes that layer (only the attributes it gives), one without id creates a layer.

parent.description: Where top-level new layers go: a frame's or page's id. Default: the current page, beside its layers.

dryRun.description: Check ids, tokens and fonts without writing; works with Allow edits off.

version.description: A name for a version saved in the file's history before writing, for the designer to go back to (not in a dry run, nor when nothing would change). Pass one before a write that changes many layers or tokens.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: execute
title: Run plugin code
description: Runs JavaScript in the Pixelwright plugin, for what design_apply and tokens_apply cannot say: the code is the body of an async function given `figma` (the Plugin API) and `console`; `return` gives `result` (layers come back as {id, type, name}, figma.mixed as "mixed"), and what it logs comes back as `logs`. What it throws comes back as `error`, with the logs before it. What it changes during the call is one undo step in Figma. Refused while the plugin's Allow edits switch is off, but code it starts that outlives the call (timers, listeners, work past the timeout) keeps running until the plugin window is closed, the switch notwithstanding. The tool waits at most 25 s; an endless loop, synchronous or of awaits, freezes Figma until the plugin is closed. Prefer the XML and token tools: they keep the file's styles and check what they write.

code.description: JavaScript run as the body of an async function with `figma` (the Plugin API) and `console`: `await` works, `return` gives the result.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the code: 10 by default, 25 at most.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: tokens_read
title: Read the design tokens
description: Reads the file's design tokens: every variable collection with all its modes (light, dark…), and the paint, text and effect styles, its own and those the current page uses from a team library, named the way design_read writes them (var(--Name)). format css (default) returns ready CSS: :root holds each collection's default mode and the styles, and every other mode is a block [data-<collection>="<mode>"] to put on the element a theme applies to; format json returns the same per collection and mode; format dtcg returns Design Tokens Format (DTCG 2025.10) trees, one per collection mode and one of styles, to save as token files for Style Dictionary or Tokens Studio. libraries: true also lists the enabled libraries' variables by name. notes say what could not be written.

collections.description: Only these variable collections, by name (case does not matter). Default: all of them.

libraries.description: Also list the enabled libraries' variables, by name and type: their values are read only once the file uses them.

used.description: Also take the styles and variables the layers on the current page (or within) use, a team library's among them. A file that uses a library has its tokens there.

within.description: The layer or page whose used tokens to take. Default: the current page.

format.description: css: ready custom properties, a block per extra mode. json: the token model, per collection and mode. dtcg: Design Tokens Format (DTCG 2025.10) trees, one per collection mode (`<collection>.<mode>`) and one of styles, each to save as its own .json file.

maxChars.description: Longest output; past it, only the summary comes back and you read collections one at a time.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

also.description: A text style's letter spacing and case, as tokens of their own.
A text style's letter spacing and case, as tokens of their own.
A text style's letter spacing and case, as tokens of their own.

name: tokens_apply
title: Write design tokens
description: Writes design tokens in the shape tokens_read returns with format json: collections with their modes and variables, each mode's value in CSS (a colour, px or a number, a quoted string, true/false, var(--token) for an alias), and styles: paint (a colour or colour variable), text (the font shorthand) and effect (a box-shadow list). Collections, modes, variables and styles are found by name among the file's own or made; what the file already holds, as tokens_read writes it, is left as it is, and nothing is deleted. A library's collection or style is never copied into the file: change it in the library. Send only what you change. errors name each variable, mode or style that could not be written while the rest goes in. One undo step in Figma; refused while the plugin's Allow edits switch is off (dryRun checks without writing).

dryRun.description: Check names, types, modes and aliases without writing; works with Allow edits off.

version.description: A name for a version saved in the file's history before writing, for the designer to go back to (not in a dry run, nor when nothing would change). Pass one before a write that changes many layers or tokens.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: version_save
title: Save a named version
description: Saves a named version in the file's Figma version history, for people: the designer can open the design as it was, and developers on a paid plan can pick it in Dev Mode's Compare changes. Save one only when the user asks: Figma's plugin API cannot list, read or delete a version, so it stays in the history. baselines: the baselines it goes with; it is saved only while the design still matches them, and they record it. Needs edit access to the file and the plugin's Allow edits; the same title is refused twice within ten minutes.

title.description: The version's name in Version history, e.g. "Built: pricing".

description.description: Shown under the title. Everyone with the file sees it: no local paths or private repository names.

baselines.description: The baselines this version goes with: it is saved only while the design still matches each one, and they record it.

file.description: A session from status, or a file name. Default: the file of the first baseline, else the active file.

id.description: The version's id; null when Figma gave none.

baselines.description: The baselines that recorded the version.

name: components_read
title: Read the components
description: Lists components: scope used (default) gives the ones the instances on the current page, or inside `within`, come from (a library's among them, with how many instances use each); scope local gives every component defined in the file. Each comes with its key, variants (a set lists its variant names, "Size=Large, State=Default"), properties with their type, default and options, and description. Use it to map Figma components to the project's code components; design_read writes instances with component, variant and props.

scope.description: used: what the page (or within) uses; local: what the file defines.

within.description: A layer or page id to look in. Default: the current page (used) or every page (local).

query.description: Only components whose name contains this.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

name: variants_read
title: Read a component's states
description: How each variant of a component set differs from its default one (the top-left, as Figma takes it), as nodes_diff says it: the attributes each changes as [the default's, this one's], the layers only one has, its properties, and the CSS pseudo-class a state value suggests (Hover → :hover, Pressed → :active, Focused → :focus-visible, Disabled → :disabled). Give the set, a variant or an instance. Build the default, then each state as its difference.

node.description: A component set's id, or one of its variants', or an instance's: its set is read.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

properties.description: Each variant property with its values.

default.description: The default variant: the top-left one, as Figma takes it.

against.description: The variant it is compared with: the one it differs from by a single property (a state first), else the default.

pseudo.description: The CSS pseudo-class a state value suggests: :hover, :active, :focus-visible, :disabled.

drawing.description: An icon's or image's own drawing differs: paths, colours, inner layers.

more.description: Variants left out: read a smaller set, or the variants one by one.

name: assets_export
title: Export assets
description: Writes files out of the design into dir. nodes: up to 50 layers, one file each (SVG for an icon, PNG at 2x otherwise, or the format and scale given; PDF too). from: every true asset inside one layer, the icons and images design_read would plan. original: the images as they were placed instead of renders (photos at full size, in their own format). The same bytes are written once, a name taken by other bytes gets -2, and a file already in dir is never overwritten with other bytes. A layer that cannot be exported is reported in errors and the rest are still written.

nodes.description: Layers to write, one file each: SVG for an icon, PNG otherwise, unless format says. Give nodes or from.

from.description: A layer to write every true asset of (its icons and images, as design_read plans them). Give nodes or from.

dir.description: The folder to write into; created if missing. Files already there are never overwritten with other bytes.

format.description: For nodes: the format of every file. WEBP is rendered as PNG by Figma and encoded here.

scale.description: For PNG, JPG and WEBP: pixels per Figma pixel, or per CSS px with width. Default 2.

width.description: For nodes as PNG, JPG or WEBP: the CSS width the build shows the layer at; the file is width × scale px wide (110 at scale 2: 220 px).

original.description: Write the images as they were placed (not cropped, filtered or scaled) instead of renders, with their real format.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

planned.description: The path design_read plans for this layer, when the file got another name: use path in its src.

name: code_connect_read
title: Read the Code Connect templates
description: Lists the project's Figma Code Connect files (templates *.figma.ts and *.figma.js, batch files *.figma.batch.json, as figma.config.json's globs name them) with what each connects on the current page, or inside `node`: components with how many instances and how each matched (by key, id or name), and what a trial run on the first gives: its error, the properties its code never reads (`unread`) and the variant values its mapping misses (`values`); `missing` marks a source file that does not exist. Also the components shown there that none connects, with the id and key a new one needs, and what keeps a file out. design_read returns their code as codeComponents. Write them with your file tools as Figma documents them (guide topic code-connect).

node.description: A layer or page id to look in, e.g. 54:243. Default: the current page.

file.description: The file to work on: its session from status or its name. Default: the active file.

root.description: The project folder the Code Connect files were looked for in.

path.description: A template file, a batch row (<batch file>#<n>), or a batch file none of whose rows is used here.

source.description: The code component's file or package, as written.

missing.description: The source names a file that does not exist.

component.description: The Figma component's (or component set's) name.

by.description: How it matched: the component's key, the id its url names, or the name.

error.description: What a trial run on the first instance it matches gave.

unread.description: Properties of that instance its code never reads: its own (Description), a nested one's (Button.Label).

values.description: Variant values its getEnum mappings miss, by property: Figma renders them as undefined.

component.description: The Figma component's (or component set's) name.

key.description: The key a batch row or // key= needs; a set's for a variant.

unconnected.description: Components shown here as layers that no Code Connect file connects.

name: guide
title: Pixelwright guide
description: How to work with Pixelwright and read what it returns. Without a topic: the topics. Topics: workflow (Which tool to use when, from finding a section to its files.); xml (The XML design_read returns: tags, metadata, CSS attributes, read-only attributes.); tokens (How tokens are named and written: styles, variables, modes, aliases, units, libraries.); assets (What becomes a file, in which format, and how files are named.); write (design_apply: changing, creating, copying and moving layers, components, instances and images with the same XML.); code-connect (Figma Code Connect templates: how design_read runs them, writing one, what Pixelwright supports.); email (Turning the XML into an HTML email that renders in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail.). Read workflow first in a new task, and xml before building from design_read.

topic.description: The topic to read. Default: the list of topics.
